fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Verbal Combat as a Martial Art", "body": "Gabe, who broadcasts as Slick Dissident, argues that the great philosophers habitually framed ideas as martial combat, claiming that Socrates was a skilled swordsman, observing that the first Academy was built on the grounds of a gymnasium, and pointing out that Schopenhauer compared debate to sword fighting. He sees the etiquette of old German fencing schools laid out inside Verbal Judo. Chance Garton adds the Celtic Ogmios, a Hercules figure whose golden chains ran from his lips to the ears of his followers, as an ancient picture of conquest through eloquence, which he calls the heart of what Verbal Judo is really about."}, {"title": "Doc Rhino and the Cost of Self-Abandonment", "body": "Chance Garton introduces George \"Doc Rhino\" Thompson, an English PhD with post-doctoral study at Princeton who, as Chance tells it, left a professorship at 35 and joined the police to learn how officers talk people down. Chance credits the method with de-escalating real conflicts, but questions its core instruction to train yourself to do the opposite of what you feel or want, arguing from his biofield tuning work that this kind of suppression carries an energetic toll. Gabe describes older seminar footage, since removed online, in which he says Thompson coached officers to abandon even their uniformed persona and switch into a machine with the mantra \"showtime baby.\""}, {"title": "Tactical Language, Names, and Self-Incrimination", "body": "Thompson's taught rule that natural language is disastrous and tactical language is a performance becomes a springboard for both hosts. Chance Garton contrasts living natural language with what he calls the dead, contract bound language of legalese, and frames citizenship as a contract to perform. Gabe argues that an officer's opening lines are designed to walk a driver past the first four amendments toward giving up the Fifth, and recalls Thompson describing naming as a kind of black magic. Gabe's counsel is to stick to those five, run the clock, and remember that the officer is the one on paid time."}, {"title": "Deflection, Paraphrasing, and Empathy", "body": "Chance Garton walks through Thompson's tools for verbal assault: mushin, or a still center under attack, protecting the other person's face, strip phrases such as \"I understand that\" followed by a redirect, and paraphrasing back exactly what was said. He calls strip phrases dishonest yet effective, while praising the principle that empathy absorbs tension, and applies these ideas to close relationships and to parenting a child at bedtime. He links them to a lesson from his biofield tuning practice, that accepting is protecting. Gabe answers by flipping the playbook, suggesting citizens repeat \"calm down\" and keep a receipt book during traffic stops."}, {"title": "Questions, Compliance, and the Inner War", "body": "Reading from Thompson's book, Chance Garton sorts question types and highlights the claim that opinion seeking questions generate compliance, which he argues extends to polling and voting. He seizes on Thompson's definition of con artistry as raising expectations in order to cheat, and retracts his own past advice to soften criticism with flattery. Gabe ties fact finding to what he calls the boondoggle, where the state keeps the benefit and the citizen keeps the liability, then lists confidence builders like knowing local lawyers and recording encounters. Chance closes by arguing that outer conflict mirrors a war between left brain and right brain."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Tonight we'll be demystifying the work of the late George "Doc Rhino" Thompson, known by police cadet trainees and corpo-ladder climbers as Verbal Judo. What are the effective tools for communication for conflict de-escalation? What do society's occult engineers know about manufacturing consent and self-incrimination? Join Slick Dissident and me for a look at the good, bad, and ugly of tactical speech.

If there's something that interests you or that you find to be rare and helpful information, save it offline.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Training yourself to do the opposite of what you feel or what you want, that is not healthy for your biofield energy, and especially if there's major cognitive dissonance that's following out of that, you're going to wind up with some sort of dysfunction, injury, disease, problem.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Another thing you have on your side is time. No, it doesn't.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "If they throw the insult at you and you don't respond to the insult, or you don't get the emotional riled up about it and then throw attack back with an insult, then the spear has now sailed harmlessly past you. It's stuck in the wall and they don't have that weapon anymore.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The power differential is an illusion. They've got these guns, they've got the armor, they've got buddies, but they are bound by duty. We have rights, which are not our... that's not our limitation.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Validating other people's experience actually gives you power in a way that our generation and the generations to come might lose their opportunities by not validating the experiences of others.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "In your internal life and internal world, the best protection you've got against other people's negative energy is being okay with the fact that they've got it. It is what it is.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I learn how they work and I realize that not only are we able to do the same, we actually can do way more than they're allowed to.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "I promise you it is safe and effective to live based on only what is a full authentic, full body hell yes, and saying no to other stuff.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Notice none of that had anything to do with life-threatening.
